source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text: {\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \textit{type} $\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\Theta$, with $|\Theta| = M$. We use $\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\Theta$ within this order, for $0\leq i < M$.

& = - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left(1 - \frac{2}{M(M-1)}\sum_{\theta_1 > \theta_2 \in \Theta} P_k(\theta_1, \theta_2)\right)\\
	&= - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \sum_{0  \leq i < j \leq M} \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\\
	&= -\max_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left( \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right)\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} 
	= \min_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( -\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \left[\log \left(\b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right]\right)\\
	&= \min_{0 \leq i < j \leq M} \inf_{a \in \mathcal{R}} \left \{ g(\theta_j) I(a|\theta_j) + g(\theta_i) I(a|\theta_i)\right\}\\

theorem source_appendix_problessthan_score_gap_rate_iid_completion
    {n m : Nat}
    [DecidableEq (finiteChainOrderedPair n)]
    (M : FiniteRatingLDPModel (Fin n) (Fin (m + 1)))
    (sampleRate : Fin n -> Real)
    (sourceModel : FiniteOrdinalSourceModel M sampleRate)
    (hpositive_sample : forall theta : Fin n, 0 < sampleRate theta)
    (hm : 1 <= m) (p : finiteChainOrderedPair n) :
    exists rate : Real,
      pairwiseSellerThresholdRateTop M sampleRate
        (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) =
          (rate : WithTop Real) /\
        ExponentialRateCertificate
          (fun k => sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb
            (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)
            (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p)
          rate := by
  let C := ordinalSourcePairwiseLdpCertificate
    M sampleRate sourceModel hpositive_sample hm
  refine ⟨C.rate p, C.threshold_rate_top_eq p, ?_⟩
  have heq : forall k,
      sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)
          (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p =
        twoSampleFloorScoreGapLeftTailProb M sampleRate
          (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k := by
    intro k
    exact source_iid_completion_weak_inversion_bridge M sampleRate p k
  refine { eventually_pos := ?_, has_rate := ?_ }
  · filter_upwards [C.leftTail p |>.eventually_pos] with k hk
    rw [heq k]
    exact hk
  · exact HasExponentialRate.congr_of_forall
      (fun k => (heq k).symm) (C.leftTail p).has_rate

    {n m : Nat}

    M sampleRate sourceModel hpositive_sample hm
  let E := C.toFloorPkComplementErrorRateCertificate
    M sampleRate finiteChainOrderedPairHi finiteChainOrderedPairLo

  have heq : forall k,

            {
              "line_end": 665,
              "line_start": 665,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "{\\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \\textit{type} $\\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\\Theta$, with $|\\Theta| = M$. We use $\\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\\Theta$ within this order, for $0\\leq i < M$.",
              "quoted_text_sha256": "4c6fe893b409d91d809b90a6fbd69d25b79034552ba9b9a28820a120929d0132"
            },
            {
              "line_end": 731,
              "line_start": 721,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "Formally, given $\\theta_1 > \\theta_2$, define $P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)$ as follows:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:Pk}\nP_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2) = \\mu_k(x_k(\\theta_1) > x_k(\\theta_2)|\\theta_1, \\theta_2) - \\mu_k(x_k(\\theta_1) < x_k(\\theta_2)|\\theta_1, \\theta_2).\n\\end{equation}\nThis expression captures the ``errors'' made by the ranking according to observed score.  In particular, when $\\theta_1 > \\theta_2$ but $x_k(\\theta_1) < x_k(\\theta_2)$, the aggregate score ranking swaps the ordering of sellers $\\theta_1$ and $\\theta_2$.  Thus, a good rating system has large $P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)$.\n\nWe consider the problem of maximizing the following objective, a scaled version of {\\em Kendall's $\\tau$ rank correlation} between the estimated ranking of sellers and the true ranking:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:objective}\nW_k = \\frac{2}{M(M-1)}\\sum_{\\theta_1 > \\theta_2 \\in \\Theta} P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)",
              "quoted_text_sha256": "570ed0ffc6d8958e85ae9fd11f3e78f6f2122f1ff62291afbd76183971bac4ff"
            },
            {
              "line_end": 1718,
              "line_start": 1714,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "\t& = - \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log \\left(1 - \\frac{2}{M(M-1)}\\sum_{\\theta_1 > \\theta_2 \\in \\Theta} P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)\\right)\\\\\n\t&= - \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log\\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \\sum_{0  \\leq i < j \\leq M} \\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\\\\n\t&= -\\max_{0\\leq i < j \\leq M}\\left( \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log \\left( \\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\right)\\right)\\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} \n\t= \\min_{0\\leq i < j \\leq M}\\left( -\\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\left[\\log \\left(\\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\right)\\right]\\right)\\\\\n\t&= \\min_{0 \\leq i < j \\leq M} \\inf_{a \\in \\mathcal{R}} \\left \\{ g(\\theta_j) I(a|\\theta_j) + g(\\theta_i) I(a|\\theta_i)\\right\\}\\\\",

              "line_end": 665,
              "line_start": 665,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "{\\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \\textit{type} $\\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\\Theta$, with $|\\Theta| = M$. We use $\\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\\Theta$ within this order, for $0\\leq i < M$.",
              "quoted_text_sha256": "4c6fe893b409d91d809b90a6fbd69d25b79034552ba9b9a28820a120929d0132"
            },
            {
              "line_end": 731,
              "line_start": 721,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "Formally, given $\\theta_1 > \\theta_2$, define $P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)$ as follows:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:Pk}\nP_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2) = \\mu_k(x_k(\\theta_1) > x_k(\\theta_2)|\\theta_1, \\theta_2) - \\mu_k(x_k(\\theta_1) < x_k(\\theta_2)|\\theta_1, \\theta_2).\n\\end{equation}\nThis expression captures the ``errors'' made by the ranking according to observed score.  In particular, when $\\theta_1 > \\theta_2$ but $x_k(\\theta_1) < x_k(\\theta_2)$, the aggregate score ranking swaps the ordering of sellers $\\theta_1$ and $\\theta_2$.  Thus, a good rating system has large $P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)$.\n\nWe consider the problem of maximizing the following objective, a scaled version of {\\em Kendall's $\\tau$ rank correlation} between the estimated ranking of sellers and the true ranking:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:objective}\nW_k = \\frac{2}{M(M-1)}\\sum_{\\theta_1 > \\theta_2 \\in \\Theta} P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)",
              "quoted_text_sha256": "570ed0ffc6d8958e85ae9fd11f3e78f6f2122f1ff62291afbd76183971bac4ff"
            },
            {
              "line_end": 1718,
              "line_start": 1714,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "\t& = - \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log \\left(1 - \\frac{2}{M(M-1)}\\sum_{\\theta_1 > \\theta_2 \\in \\Theta} P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)\\right)\\\\\n\t&= - \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log\\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \\sum_{0  \\leq i < j \\leq M} \\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\\\\n\t&= -\\max_{0\\leq i < j \\leq M}\\left( \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log \\left( \\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\right)\\right)\\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} \n\t= \\min_{0\\leq i < j \\leq M}\\left( -\\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\left[\\log \\left(\\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\right)\\right]\\right)\\\\\n\t&= \\min_{0 \\leq i < j \\leq M} \\inf_{a \\in \\mathcal{R}} \\left \\{ g(\\theta_j) I(a|\\theta_j) + g(\\theta_i) I(a|\\theta_i)\\right\\}\\\\",

    "lean_source_declaration": "theorem source_appendix_problessthan_score_gap_rate_iid_completion\n    {n m : Nat}\n    [DecidableEq (finiteChainOrderedPair n)]\n    (M : FiniteRatingLDPModel (Fin n) (Fin (m + 1)))\n    (sampleRate : Fin n -> Real)\n    (sourceModel : FiniteOrdinalSourceModel M sampleRate)\n    (hpositive_sample : forall theta : Fin n, 0 < sampleRate theta)\n    (hm : 1 <= m) (p : finiteChainOrderedPair n) :\n    exists rate : Real,\n      pairwiseSellerThresholdRateTop M sampleRate\n        (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) =\n          (rate : WithTop Real) /\\\n        ExponentialRateCertificate\n          (fun k => sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb\n            (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)\n            (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p)\n          rate := by\n  let C := ordinalSourcePairwiseLdpCertificate\n    M sampleRate sourceModel hpositive_sample hm\n  refine \u27e8C.rate p, C.threshold_rate_top_eq p, ?_\u27e9\n  have heq : forall k,\n      sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)\n          (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p =\n        twoSampleFloorScoreGapLeftTailProb M sampleRate\n          (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k := by\n    intro k\n    exact source_iid_completion_weak_inversion_bridge M sampleRate p k\n  refine { eventually_pos := ?_, has_rate := ?_ }\n  \u00b7 filter_upwards [C.leftTail p |>.eventually_pos] with k hk\n    rw [heq k]\n    exact hk\n  \u00b7 exact HasExponentialRate.congr_of_forall\n      (fun k => (heq k).symm) (C.leftTail p).has_rate",

    "lean_source_declaration": "theorem source_appendix_pk_ld_complement_rate_iid_completion\n    {n m : Nat}\n    [DecidableEq (finiteChainOrderedPair n)]\n    (M : FiniteRatingLDPModel (Fin n) (Fin (m + 1)))\n    (sampleRate : Fin n -> Real)\n    (sourceModel : FiniteOrdinalSourceModel M sampleRate)\n    (hpositive_sample : forall theta : Fin n, 0 < sampleRate theta)\n    (hm : 1 <= m) (p : finiteChainOrderedPair n) :\n    exists rate : Real,\n      pairwiseSellerThresholdRateTop M sampleRate\n        (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) =\n          (rate : WithTop Real) /\\\n        ExponentialRateCertificate\n          (fun k => 1 - sourceStatePairwisePk\n            (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)\n            (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p)\n          rate := by\n  let C := ordinalSourcePairwiseLdpCertificate\n    M sampleRate sourceModel hpositive_sample hm\n  let E := C.toFloorPkComplementErrorRateCertificate\n    M sampleRate finiteChainOrderedPairHi finiteChainOrderedPairLo\n  refine \u27e8C.rate p, C.threshold_rate_top_eq p, ?_\u27e9\n  have heq : forall k,\n      1 - sourceStatePairwisePk (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)\n          (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p =\n        twoSampleFloorPkComplementErrorProb M sampleRate\n          (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k := by\n    intro k\n    rw [source_iid_completion_pairwise_objective_bridge]\n    exact (twoSampleFloorPkComplementErrorProb_eq_one_sub_pkObjectiveProb\n      M sampleRate (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k).symm\n  refine { eventually_pos := ?_, has_rate := ?_ }\n  \u00b7 filter_upwards [E.has_rate p |>.eventually_pos] with k hk\n    rw [heq k]\n    exact hk\n  \u00b7 exact HasExponentialRate.congr_of_forall\n      (fun k => (heq k).symm) (E.has_rate p).has_rate",

    {n m : Nat}
    [DecidableEq (finiteChainOrderedPair n)]
    (M : FiniteRatingLDPModel (Fin n) (Fin (m + 1)))
    (sampleRate : Fin n -> Real)
    (sourceModel : FiniteOrdinalSourceModel M sampleRate)
    (hpositive_sample : forall theta : Fin n, 0 < sampleRate theta)
    (hm : 1 <= m) (p : finiteChainOrderedPair n) :
    exists rate : Real,
      pairwiseSellerThresholdRateTop M sampleRate
        (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) =
          (rate : WithTop Real) /\
        ExponentialRateCertificate
          (fun k => sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb
            (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)
            (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p)
          rate := by
  let C := ordinalSourcePairwiseLdpCertificate
    M sampleRate sourceModel hpositive_sample hm
  refine ⟨C.rate p, C.threshold_rate_top_eq p, ?_⟩
  have heq : forall k,
      sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)
          (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p =
        twoSampleFloorScoreGapLeftTailProb M sampleRate
          (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k := by
    intro k
    exact source_iid_completion_weak_inversion_bridge M sampleRate p k
  refine { eventually_pos := ?_, has_rate := ?_ }
  · filter_upwards [C.leftTail p |>.eventually_pos] with k hk
    rw [heq k]
    exact hk
  · exact HasExponentialRate.congr_of_forall
      (fun k => (heq k).symm) (C.leftTail p).has_rate

semantic_context_requirements.explanation: The source orders its finite seller-type carrier as theta_i, then defines P_k only given theta_1 > theta_2 and sums only those pairs in W_k; its proof rewrites that aggregate as i < j with P_k(theta_j, theta_i). Review a Lean restricted pair carrier as exactly one finite high/low pair with strict low < high, not as a theorem for arbitrary, equal, or reversed seller pairs and not as an unrecorded model assumption.

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text: {\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \textit{type} $\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\Theta$, with $|\Theta| = M$. We use $\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\Theta$ within this order, for $0\leq i < M$.

& = - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left(1 - \frac{2}{M(M-1)}\sum_{\theta_1 > \theta_2 \in \Theta} P_k(\theta_1, \theta_2)\right)\\
	&= - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \sum_{0  \leq i < j \leq M} \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\\
	&= -\max_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left( \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right)\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} 
	= \min_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( -\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \left[\log \left(\b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right]\right)\\
	&= \min_{0 \leq i < j \leq M} \inf_{a \in \mathcal{R}} \left \{ g(\theta_j) I(a|\theta_j) + g(\theta_i) I(a|\theta_i)\right\}\\

    {n m : Nat}
    [DecidableEq (finiteChainOrderedPair n)]
    (M : FiniteRatingLDPModel (Fin n) (Fin (m + 1)))
    (sampleRate : Fin n -> Real)
    (sourceModel : FiniteOrdinalSourceModel M sampleRate)
    (hpositive_sample : forall theta : Fin n, 0 < sampleRate theta)
    (hm : 1 <= m) (p : finiteChainOrderedPair n) :
    exists rate : Real,
      pairwiseSellerThresholdRateTop M sampleRate
        (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) =

            (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)

    M sampleRate sourceModel hpositive_sample hm

      sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)
          (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p =
        twoSampleFloorScoreGapLeftTailProb M sampleRate

    rw [heq k]

dimensions.required_check: Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. When the generated surface requests a cardinality-boundary analysis, record the source and Lean cardinal domains, every smallest/endpoint case checked, and either the strictness witness or a semantic reason no such witness is needed. A theorem, wrapper, or carrier name is not that analysis. A local opaque/constant/axiom carrier must expose a checked refinement before it is treated as ordinary model data.

For a finite/ordered probabilistic model, derive support at each endpoint from the source condition actually stated. Strict adjacent-tail comparisons do not by themselves supply a terminal cutoff or positive top/bottom atom; inspect zero mass, degenerate, and boundary cases separately.

Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. If either side sorts, ranks, relabels, or quotients samples before computing an outcome, prove the corresponding pushforward and outcome-equivariance bridge; matching marginal tables or an informal exchangeability argument is not enough. When the generated surface requests transformed-law analysis, record the source and Lean operations, the full parameter domain including sign/zero endpoints, normalization or pushforward evidence, and outcome-equivariance evidence (or an explicit semantic no-transform/no-relabeling finding). Separately write the source and Lean distribution parameterizations: the exact scale/rate/precision/standard-deviation/variance convention, the parameter mapping formula, and a checked law equality or outcome-preservation bridge. A positive reparameterization or matching declaration name is not a law-equivalence argument.

State exactly whether source and Lean use a pointwise conditional law, an almost-everywhere conditional version, positive-fiber identities, or measurable-event calibration. Expand the event, sigma-algebra/measurability, and joint-law formula; a statement about exact fibers does not silently determine atomless or null fibers. Any switch among these semantics needs a Lean-checked bridge, not a source-looking conditional-probability or calibration name.

For every source or Lean expectation/integral reached through this model, identify the law and integrand and establish the exact definedness convention: measurability or a.e.-measurability, integrability/finite integral, or an explicitly extended-value integral. For every conditioning/partition formula reached through this model, compare finite, countable, and arbitrary partition scope; cell measurability, disjointness, and cover on the relevant support; and the value assigned when a cell has zero mass. Expand every ratio/branch used to totalize zero denominators. A finite measurable-cell proof or a positive-mass-only identity does not cover an advertised arbitrary partition without a Lean-checked refinement.

Compare the source rate codomain with the Lean codomain after unfolding the rate definition. A Real-valued formula is not automatically a WithTop/extended-real statement: account for eventual-zero events, infinite rates, zero sample counts, and boundary minimizers.

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text: {\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \textit{type} $\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\Theta$, with $|\Theta| = M$. We use $\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\Theta$ within this order, for $0\leq i < M$.

& = - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left(1 - \frac{2}{M(M-1)}\sum_{\theta_1 > \theta_2 \in \Theta} P_k(\theta_1, \theta_2)\right)\\
	&= - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \sum_{0  \leq i < j \leq M} \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\\
	&= -\max_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left( \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right)\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} 
	= \min_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( -\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \left[\log \left(\b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right]\right)\\
	&= \min_{0 \leq i < j \leq M} \inf_{a \in \mathcal{R}} \left \{ g(\theta_j) I(a|\theta_j) + g(\theta_i) I(a|\theta_i)\right\}\\

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text: {\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \textit{type} $\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\Theta$, with $|\Theta| = M$. We use $\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\Theta$ within this order, for $0\leq i < M$.

& = - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left(1 - \frac{2}{M(M-1)}\sum_{\theta_1 > \theta_2 \in \Theta} P_k(\theta_1, \theta_2)\right)\\
	&= - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \sum_{0  \leq i < j \leq M} \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\\
	&= -\max_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left( \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right)\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} 
	= \min_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( -\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \left[\log \left(\b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right]\right)\\
	&= \min_{0 \leq i < j \leq M} \inf_{a \in \mathcal{R}} \left \{ g(\theta_j) I(a|\theta_j) + g(\theta_i) I(a|\theta_i)\right\}\\

              "line_end": 665,
              "line_start": 665,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "{\\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \\textit{type} $\\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\\Theta$, with $|\\Theta| = M$. We use $\\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\\Theta$ within this order, for $0\\leq i < M$.",
              "quoted_text_sha256": "4c6fe893b409d91d809b90a6fbd69d25b79034552ba9b9a28820a120929d0132"
            },
            {
              "line_end": 731,
              "line_start": 721,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "Formally, given $\\theta_1 > \\theta_2$, define $P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)$ as follows:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:Pk}\nP_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2) = \\mu_k(x_k(\\theta_1) > x_k(\\theta_2)|\\theta_1, \\theta_2) - \\mu_k(x_k(\\theta_1) < x_k(\\theta_2)|\\theta_1, \\theta_2).\n\\end{equation}\nThis expression captures the ``errors'' made by the ranking according to observed score.  In particular, when $\\theta_1 > \\theta_2$ but $x_k(\\theta_1) < x_k(\\theta_2)$, the aggregate score ranking swaps the ordering of sellers $\\theta_1$ and $\\theta_2$.  Thus, a good rating system has large $P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)$.\n\nWe consider the problem of maximizing the following objective, a scaled version of {\\em Kendall's $\\tau$ rank correlation} between the estimated ranking of sellers and the true ranking:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:objective}\nW_k = \\frac{2}{M(M-1)}\\sum_{\\theta_1 > \\theta_2 \\in \\Theta} P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)",
              "quoted_text_sha256": "570ed0ffc6d8958e85ae9fd11f3e78f6f2122f1ff62291afbd76183971bac4ff"
            },
            {
              "line_end": 1718,
              "line_start": 1714,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "\t& = - \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log \\left(1 - \\frac{2}{M(M-1)}\\sum_{\\theta_1 > \\theta_2 \\in \\Theta} P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)\\right)\\\\\n\t&= - \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log\\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \\sum_{0  \\leq i < j \\leq M} \\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\\\\n\t&= -\\max_{0\\leq i < j \\leq M}\\left( \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log \\left( \\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\right)\\right)\\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} \n\t= \\min_{0\\leq i < j \\leq M}\\left( -\\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\left[\\log \\left(\\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\right)\\right]\\right)\\\\\n\t&= \\min_{0 \\leq i < j \\leq M} \\inf_{a \\in \\mathcal{R}} \\left \\{ g(\\theta_j) I(a|\\theta_j) + g(\\theta_i) I(a|\\theta_i)\\right\\}\\\\",
              "quoted_text_sha256": "474978bf045aafe2a2a6b185eb8d3952c502505ea13ff956bd6ec6b9e1374657"
            }

              "line_end": 665,
              "line_start": 665,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "{\\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \\textit{type} $\\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\\Theta$, with $|\\Theta| = M$. We use $\\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\\Theta$ within this order, for $0\\leq i < M$.",
              "quoted_text_sha256": "4c6fe893b409d91d809b90a6fbd69d25b79034552ba9b9a28820a120929d0132"
            },
            {
              "line_end": 731,
              "line_start": 721,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "Formally, given $\\theta_1 > \\theta_2$, define $P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)$ as follows:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:Pk}\nP_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2) = \\mu_k(x_k(\\theta_1) > x_k(\\theta_2)|\\theta_1, \\theta_2) - \\mu_k(x_k(\\theta_1) < x_k(\\theta_2)|\\theta_1, \\theta_2).\n\\end{equation}\nThis expression captures the ``errors'' made by the ranking according to observed score.  In particular, when $\\theta_1 > \\theta_2$ but $x_k(\\theta_1) < x_k(\\theta_2)$, the aggregate score ranking swaps the ordering of sellers $\\theta_1$ and $\\theta_2$.  Thus, a good rating system has large $P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)$.\n\nWe consider the problem of maximizing the following objective, a scaled version of {\\em Kendall's $\\tau$ rank correlation} between the estimated ranking of sellers and the true ranking:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:objective}\nW_k = \\frac{2}{M(M-1)}\\sum_{\\theta_1 > \\theta_2 \\in \\Theta} P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)",
              "quoted_text_sha256": "570ed0ffc6d8958e85ae9fd11f3e78f6f2122f1ff62291afbd76183971bac4ff"
            },
            {
              "line_end": 1718,
              "line_start": 1714,
              "path": "cited publication",
              "quoted_text": "\t& = - \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log \\left(1 - \\frac{2}{M(M-1)}\\sum_{\\theta_1 > \\theta_2 \\in \\Theta} P_k(\\theta_1, \\theta_2)\\right)\\\\\n\t&= - \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log\\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \\sum_{0  \\leq i < j \\leq M} \\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\\\\n\t&= -\\max_{0\\leq i < j \\leq M}\\left( \\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\log \\left( \\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\right)\\right)\\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} \n\t= \\min_{0\\leq i < j \\leq M}\\left( -\\lim_{k \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{k} \\left[\\log \\left(\\b{P}_k(\\theta_j, \\theta_i)\\right)\\right]\\right)\\\\\n\t&= \\min_{0 \\leq i < j \\leq M} \\inf_{a \\in \\mathcal{R}} \\left \\{ g(\\theta_j) I(a|\\theta_j) + g(\\theta_i) I(a|\\theta_i)\\right\\}\\\\",

            }

    "lean_source_declaration": "theorem source_appendix_problessthan_score_gap_rate_iid_completion\n    {n m : Nat}\n    [DecidableEq (finiteChainOrderedPair n)]\n    (M : FiniteRatingLDPModel (Fin n) (Fin (m + 1)))\n    (sampleRate : Fin n -> Real)\n    (sourceModel : FiniteOrdinalSourceModel M sampleRate)\n    (hpositive_sample : forall theta : Fin n, 0 < sampleRate theta)\n    (hm : 1 <= m) (p : finiteChainOrderedPair n) :\n    exists rate : Real,\n      pairwiseSellerThresholdRateTop M sampleRate\n        (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) =\n          (rate : WithTop Real) /\\\n        ExponentialRateCertificate\n          (fun k => sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb\n            (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)\n            (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p)\n          rate := by\n  let C := ordinalSourcePairwiseLdpCertificate\n    M sampleRate sourceModel hpositive_sample hm\n  refine \u27e8C.rate p, C.threshold_rate_top_eq p, ?_\u27e9\n  have heq : forall k,\n      sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)\n          (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p =\n        twoSampleFloorScoreGapLeftTailProb M sampleRate\n          (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k := by\n    intro k\n    exact source_iid_completion_weak_inversion_bridge M sampleRate p k\n  refine { eventually_pos := ?_, has_rate := ?_ }\n  \u00b7 filter_upwards [C.leftTail p |>.eventually_pos] with k hk\n    rw [heq k]\n    exact hk\n  \u00b7 exact HasExponentialRate.congr_of_forall\n      (fun k => (heq k).symm) (C.leftTail p).has_rate",

    "lean_source_declaration": "theorem source_appendix_pk_ld_complement_rate_iid_completion\n    {n m : Nat}\n    [DecidableEq (finiteChainOrderedPair n)]\n    (M : FiniteRatingLDPModel (Fin n) (Fin (m + 1)))\n    (sampleRate : Fin n -> Real)\n    (sourceModel : FiniteOrdinalSourceModel M sampleRate)\n    (hpositive_sample : forall theta : Fin n, 0 < sampleRate theta)\n    (hm : 1 <= m) (p : finiteChainOrderedPair n) :\n    exists rate : Real,\n      pairwiseSellerThresholdRateTop M sampleRate\n        (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) =\n          (rate : WithTop Real) /\\\n        ExponentialRateCertificate\n          (fun k => 1 - sourceStatePairwisePk\n            (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)\n            (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p)\n          rate := by\n  let C := ordinalSourcePairwiseLdpCertificate\n    M sampleRate sourceModel hpositive_sample hm\n  let E := C.toFloorPkComplementErrorRateCertificate\n    M sampleRate finiteChainOrderedPairHi finiteChainOrderedPairLo\n  refine \u27e8C.rate p, C.threshold_rate_top_eq p, ?_\u27e9\n  have heq : forall k,\n      1 - sourceStatePairwisePk (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)\n          (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p =\n        twoSampleFloorPkComplementErrorProb M sampleRate\n          (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k := by\n    intro k\n    rw [source_iid_completion_pairwise_objective_bridge]\n    exact (twoSampleFloorPkComplementErrorProb_eq_one_sub_pkObjectiveProb\n      M sampleRate (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k).symm\n  refine { eventually_pos := ?_, has_rate := ?_ }\n  \u00b7 filter_upwards [E.has_rate p |>.eventually_pos] with k hk\n    rw [heq k]\n    exact hk\n  \u00b7 exact HasExponentialRate.congr_of_forall\n      (fun k => (heq k).symm) (E.has_rate p).has_rate",

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text: {\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \textit{type} $\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\Theta$, with $|\Theta| = M$. We use $\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\Theta$ within this order, for $0\leq i < M$.

& = - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left(1 - \frac{2}{M(M-1)}\sum_{\theta_1 > \theta_2 \in \Theta} P_k(\theta_1, \theta_2)\right)\\
	&= - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \sum_{0  \leq i < j \leq M} \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\\
	&= -\max_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left( \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right)\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} 
	= \min_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( -\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \left[\log \left(\b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right]\right)\\
	&= \min_{0 \leq i < j \leq M} \inf_{a \in \mathcal{R}} \left \{ g(\theta_j) I(a|\theta_j) + g(\theta_i) I(a|\theta_i)\right\}\\

theorem source_appendix_pk_ld_complement_rate_iid_completion
    {n m : Nat}
    [DecidableEq (finiteChainOrderedPair n)]
    (M : FiniteRatingLDPModel (Fin n) (Fin (m + 1)))
    (sampleRate : Fin n -> Real)
    (sourceModel : FiniteOrdinalSourceModel M sampleRate)
    (hpositive_sample : forall theta : Fin n, 0 < sampleRate theta)
    (hm : 1 <= m) (p : finiteChainOrderedPair n) :
    exists rate : Real,
      pairwiseSellerThresholdRateTop M sampleRate
        (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) =
          (rate : WithTop Real) /\
        ExponentialRateCertificate
          (fun k => 1 - sourceStatePairwisePk
            (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)
            (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p)
          rate := by
  let C := ordinalSourcePairwiseLdpCertificate
    M sampleRate sourceModel hpositive_sample hm
  let E := C.toFloorPkComplementErrorRateCertificate
    M sampleRate finiteChainOrderedPairHi finiteChainOrderedPairLo

  have heq : forall k,
      1 - sourceStatePairwisePk (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)
          (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p =
        twoSampleFloorPkComplementErrorProb M sampleRate
          (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k := by
    intro k
    rw [source_iid_completion_pairwise_objective_bridge]
    exact (twoSampleFloorPkComplementErrorProb_eq_one_sub_pkObjectiveProb
      M sampleRate (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k).symm

      (fun k => (heq k).symm) (E.has_rate p).has_rate

theorem source_appendix_problessthan_score_gap_rate_iid_completion
    {n m : Nat}
    [DecidableEq (finiteChainOrderedPair n)]
    (M : FiniteRatingLDPModel (Fin n) (Fin (m + 1)))
    (sampleRate : Fin n -> Real)
    (sourceModel : FiniteOrdinalSourceModel M sampleRate)
    (hpositive_sample : forall theta : Fin n, 0 < sampleRate theta)
    (hm : 1 <= m) (p : finiteChainOrderedPair n) :
    exists rate : Real,
      pairwiseSellerThresholdRateTop M sampleRate
        (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) =
          (rate : WithTop Real) /\
        ExponentialRateCertificate
          (fun k => sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb
            (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)
            (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p)
          rate := by
  let C := ordinalSourcePairwiseLdpCertificate
    M sampleRate sourceModel hpositive_sample hm
  refine ⟨C.rate p, C.threshold_rate_top_eq p, ?_⟩
  have heq : forall k,
      sourceStateScoreGapLeftTailProb (iidFloorSourceStateLaw M sampleRate k)
          (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p =
        twoSampleFloorScoreGapLeftTailProb M sampleRate
          (finiteChainOrderedPairHi p) (finiteChainOrderedPairLo p) k := by
    intro k
    exact source_iid_completion_weak_inversion_bridge M sampleRate p k
  refine { eventually_pos := ?_, has_rate := ?_ }
  · filter_upwards [C.leftTail p |>.eventually_pos] with k hk
    rw [heq k]
    exact hk
  · exact HasExponentialRate.congr_of_forall
      (fun k => (heq k).symm) (C.leftTail p).has_rate

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text: {\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \textit{type} $\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\Theta$, with $|\Theta| = M$. We use $\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\Theta$ within this order, for $0\leq i < M$.

& = - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left(1 - \frac{2}{M(M-1)}\sum_{\theta_1 > \theta_2 \in \Theta} P_k(\theta_1, \theta_2)\right)\\
	&= - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \sum_{0  \leq i < j \leq M} \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\\
	&= -\max_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left( \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right)\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} 
	= \min_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( -\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \left[\log \left(\b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right]\right)\\
	&= \min_{0 \leq i < j \leq M} \inf_{a \in \mathcal{R}} \left \{ g(\theta_j) I(a|\theta_j) + g(\theta_i) I(a|\theta_i)\right\}\\

          (iidFloorSourceStateScore M sampleRate k) p =

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text: {\bf Sellers}.  The system consists of a unit mass of sellers, each associated with a quality \textit{type} $\theta$, which is (initially) unknown to the platform. We assume $\theta$ is drawn independently and uniformly at random from a finite and totally ordered set $\Theta$, with $|\Theta| = M$. We use $\theta_i$ to denote the $i$th element of $\Theta$ within this order, for $0\leq i < M$.

& = - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left(1 - \frac{2}{M(M-1)}\sum_{\theta_1 > \theta_2 \in \Theta} P_k(\theta_1, \theta_2)\right)\\
	&= - \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log\frac{2}{M(M-1)} \sum_{0  \leq i < j \leq M} \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\\
	&= -\max_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \log \left( \b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right)\label{eqnstep:ldpproperty} 
	= \min_{0\leq i < j \leq M}\left( -\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \left[\log \left(\b{P}_k(\theta_j, \theta_i)\right)\right]\right)\\
	&= \min_{0 \leq i < j \leq M} \inf_{a \in \mathcal{R}} \left \{ g(\theta_j) I(a|\theta_j) + g(\theta_i) I(a|\theta_i)\right\}\\
